topic: lining and planting a wildlife pond in a garden

provenance.author: glowny-en-b
provenance.notes: 10 turns, user first; variant a is liner sizing, pricing and planting arithmetic with closed task questions, base is an exploratory dialogue about fitting the liner and planting for frogs and newts. Grounded external referent: the liner, introduced in turn 0 (heavy roll on a pole) and mentioned in the sentence directly before every insertion (pole, sand bed, heavy roll, settling, open on boards).

a: Here is the pond dig, and the liner size needs working out before anything is ordered.
The hole is four metres long, three metres wide, and eighty centimetres deep at the middle.
The liner rule adds twice the depth to each side, plus half a metre of overlap all round.
Work out the liner length first and then the width from those same figures.
How many metres long must the liner be once the rule is applied in full?
base: The pond dig is finished at last, with two shelves and a deep middle for the winter.
We want frogs and newts rather than fish, so everything follows from that choice.
The liner arrived rolled on a pole, and it is heavier than the two of us expected.
The forecast gives us one dry week before the autumn rain sets in properly.
What should happen to the hole itself before the liner ever goes near it?

a: The length comes to six point six metres once both depths and both overlaps are added.
The width comes to five point six metres by the same rule applied across.
Rounded up to the half metre for ordering, that is seven by six exactly.
The underlay is cut to the same figures, so one order covers both sheets.
Does a seven by six sheet match the sizes listed on the supplier page?
base: Walk the hole on your knees and pull out every stone, root and old nail you find.
Then rake the surface smooth and pack a thin bed of soft sand over the base.
Underlay goes over the sand as a second skin before anything heavier arrives.
The liner only ever sees what the sand bed failed to cover underneath it.
Have you checked the shelves are level all round with a plank and a spirit level?

a: Now price the order, because the liner costs twelve pounds for each square metre.
The underlay costs three pounds for each square metre at the same shop.
The sand comes in twenty-five kilogram bags, and the base needs eight bags in all.
Each sand bag costs four pounds, and delivery is a flat fifteen pounds on top.
Keep every price in whole pounds and carry the delivery charge to the end.
What does the liner sheet alone cost at seven metres by six?
base: The shelves came out level along the plank, near enough all the way round.
The liner is what worries me now, because the roll weighs more than a sack of cement.
The sand went down this morning and the underlay is cut and waiting in the shed.
There are only two of us here, and the hole is wider than our arms can reach.
How do two people get a heavy sheet centred without dragging it across the sand?

a: The liner sheet is forty-two square metres, and at twelve pounds that comes to five hundred four.
The underlay at three pounds over the same area adds one hundred twenty-six pounds.
Eight bags of sand at four pounds each put another thirty-two pounds on the bill.
With the flat fifteen for delivery, the order stands at six hundred seventy-seven pounds.
Does that six hundred seventy-seven sit inside the budget you set for the whole pond?
base: Unroll the liner on the lawn first and refold it into a loose parcel you can carry.
Set the parcel on boards laid across the hole, then open it out from the middle.
The liner should settle under its own weight while you keep your boots off the sand.
Let the water do the fitting, because a filling pond pulls the sheet into every corner.
Do you have enough stored rainwater, or will the first fill come from the tap?

a: One correction to the dig figures: the depth at the middle is ninety centimetres, not eighty.
Rework the liner length and width with the deeper figure and keep the overlap the same.
Then round both figures up to the half metre for the order as before.
Leave the underlay at the old size, because that sheet is already cut.
Which new length does the rule give before any rounding is applied to it?
base: We have three water butts full of rainwater, about six hundred litres between them.
The tap water here is hard, and the man at the nursery pulled a face at it.
The folds at the corners look big and ugly to us both this evening.
The liner is lying open across the boards, ready for the first bucket tomorrow.
Should the corner folds be pleated flat now, or left for the water to press?

a: The rule gives six point eight metres of length with the ninety centimetre depth in place.
The width becomes five point eight metres by the same working across the hole.
Both round up to seven and six, so the ordered sheet does not change at all.
The bill therefore stays at six hundred seventy-seven pounds as already totalled.
Does any line of the order need changing after that deeper measurement is applied?
base: Pleat the two worst corners into single flat folds and point them away from the sun.
Pressed folds trap less silt and give the newts fewer blind pockets to squeeze into.
Start the rainwater slowly and let the liner creep down the shelves as it fills.
Six hundred litres will cover the base and hold the sheet for the first night.
What is the plan for topping up once the butts have run dry?

a: Now count the plants, because the nursery sells them in baskets of three.
The shallow shelf takes nine marsh plants and the deep shelf takes six.
The deep middle takes three pondweed bundles, sold loose rather than in baskets.
Keep the pondweed off the basket count and list it on its own line.
Work out how many baskets of three the two shelves need between them.
How many baskets must be ordered so neither shelf comes up short?
base: Topping up can wait for rain, because a wildlife pond is allowed to rise and fall.
The nursery list is long, and we do not know the difference between half of it.
The shallow shelf wants marsh marigold and the deep shelf wants something for the newts.
Everyone says oxygen plants matter most, and everyone names a different one to buy.
Which plants actually earn their keep in a pond dug for frogs and newts?

a: The two shelves take fifteen plants in all, nine shallow and six deep.
Fifteen divided into baskets of three comes to five baskets exactly, with none spare.
The pondweed goes on its own line as three loose bundles, as instructed.
The order therefore reads five baskets of three plus three loose bundles of pondweed.
Should a spare basket be added in case one arrives damaged in the van?
base: Marsh marigold earns its place, and so does water forget-me-not along the shallow shelf.
For the deep shelf take hornwort, which sinks and keeps the water clear without any planting.
Newts lay eggs in the forget-me-not leaves, folding each one over like a parcel.
Skip anything the nursery calls vigorous, because vigorous in a small pond means everywhere.
How much of the water surface do you want covered by summer, roughly?

a: Print the planting day as four jobs in order for the two of us.
Job one is baskets, job two is the shelves, job three is pondweed, job four is edges.
Work starts at ten in the morning and each job takes forty-five minutes.
Add a fifteen minute break after the second job and none after the others.
Which clock time does the pondweed job begin once that break is included?
base: About a third covered sounds right to us, with clear water over the deep middle.
The frogspawn question can wait until spring, when the local ponds are full of it.
The edges still show a white rim of bare sheet above the waterline all round.
We have turf offcuts and a pile of flat stones to play with.
What is the kindest way to hide that rim before the first frost?

a: The baskets run from ten until quarter to eleven, and the shelves follow straight on.
The shelves finish at half past eleven, and the break runs to quarter to twelve.
The pondweed job begins at quarter to twelve and ends at half past twelve.
The edges close the day from half past twelve until quarter past one.
All four jobs and the break fit inside three and a quarter hours taken together.
base: Tuck the rim under turf offcuts on the sunny side, green side up to the water.
Use the flat stones on the shady side, stacked to make a shallow beach for climbing out.
A hedgehog that falls in must be able to walk out, so keep one slope gentle.
Leave the rest of the rim alone, because plants will lean over it by June.
After that, the pond does the finishing better than either of you ever could.
